config.title: rem and em

intro.title: rem and em
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with text elements to understand and apply the CSS units 'rem' and 'em'. You will learn how 'rem' is based on the root element's font size and 'em' is relative to its parent element's font size. The core concept involves using these relative units to create scalable and maintainable designs. You will work with CSS properties like font-size, padding, and margin. By the end, you'll be able to control spacing and sizing in a flexible way that adapts to different screen sizes and user preferences.
intro.usecase: The rem and em units are essential for building scalable and accessible user interfaces in real-world web applications. For example, in a responsive dashboard, developers use rem to set a consistent base font size for the entire layout, ensuring that all elements scale proportionally when a user adjusts their browser's default font settings. Within a complex navigation menu or a modal component, em units are used to size padding, margins, and font sizes relative to their parent container, allowing nested elements like buttons or icons to adapt seamlessly when the menu's font size changes. This approach is critical in design systems and component libraries, where maintaining visual harmony and accessibility across different screen sizes and user preferences is a key requirement for professional front-end development.

objectives: Apply rem units to set font sizes relative to the root element.
Configure padding and margins using em units for scalable spacing.
Construct a responsive layout by combining rem and em for typography and components.
Manipulate element sizing by adjusting the root font-size to test rem scaling.
Integrate em units within nested elements to observe inheritance effects.
Update a CSS stylesheet to replace pixel values with relative units.
Control component dimensions using rem for consistent scaling across the viewport.

steps.title: Link the CSS file and set base font size
steps.instruction: Add a link element inside the head section to connect your CSS file, and set the html element's font-size to 16px to establish the root for rem calculations.
steps.hint: Use a <link> tag with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css' inside the <head>. Then, in the CSS, target the html selector and set font-size: 16px;.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- HTML head section -->
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>

/* CSS file */
html {
  font-size: 16px;
}
steps.seedCode:

/* Add your CSS rules below */
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file will have a linked CSS stylesheet, and the CSS will set the root font size to 16px, enabling consistent rem unit calculations.
successCriteria: A link element with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css' is present in the head, and the CSS contains html { font-size: 16px; }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the link element in HTML and the html { font-size: 16px; } rule in CSS are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the link element inside the head with the correct attributes, and that your CSS targets the html element to set the base font size.

steps.title: Style the container with rem units for padding
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a container class that sets padding to 2rem.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .container and the padding property with the value 2rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container class will have padding set to 2rem, creating spacing relative to the root font size.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the padding property with the value 2rem inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container class should have padding set to 2rem. Check that you've used the correct property and value.

steps.title: Style the main heading with rem units for font size
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the h1 element that sets its font-size to 2.5rem.
steps.hint: Create a selector for h1 and use the font-size property with the value 2.5rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 element will have a font size that is 2.5 times the root font size (16px by default), making it 40px.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule for h1 with font-size: 2.5rem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct selector (h1) and property (font-size: 2.5rem).
steps.feedbackWrong: create a rule for h1 that sets font-size to 2.5rem.

steps.title: Style the paragraph with rem units for margin
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the paragraph element that sets a bottom margin of 1.5rem.
steps.hint: Use the 'p' selector and the 'margin-bottom' property with the value '1.5rem'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph will have proportional vertical spacing below it based on the root font size.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for 'p' with 'margin-bottom: 1.5rem' is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the 'p' selector and setting 'margin-bottom' to '1.5rem'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph rule is missing or incorrect. Try adding 'p { margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }'.

steps.title: Create a nested element and set its font size with em units
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a span element inside the paragraph, setting its font-size to 1.5em.
steps.hint: Target the span element with a selector like 'p span' and use the property font-size: 1.5em;
steps.expectedOutcome: The span element will have a font size that is 1.5 times the font size of its parent paragraph.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for 'p span' with font-size: 1.5em is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've correctly targeted the span inside the paragraph and used the exact value 1.5em.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for the span with em units is missing or incorrect. Please add a rule for 'p span' with font-size: 1.5em.

steps.title: Apply em units for padding on the nested element
steps.instruction: Add padding to the existing span rule using em units to create padding proportional to the span's font size.
steps.hint: Add a padding property to the span selector with a value like 0.5em.
steps.expectedOutcome: The span element will have padding that scales with its font size, demonstrating how em units work for properties other than font-size.
successCriteria: The span selector includes a padding property with a value using em units.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added padding with em units to the span selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The span rule should include padding with em units. Try adding something like padding: 0.5em; to the existing span selector.

steps.title: Create a button and style it with em units for all dimensions
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a button element that uses em units for padding, font-size, and border-radius to create proportional scaling. Use the values: padding: 0.75em 1.5em, font-size: 1em, border-radius: 0.5em.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector for 'button' and apply the specified em-based properties. Remember that em units scale relative to the element's own font-size.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element will be styled with proportional padding, font-size, and border-radius using em units, demonstrating how em scales dimensions relative to font-size.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a button selector with padding: 0.75em 1.5em, font-size: 1em, and border-radius: 0.5em.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all three properties with the exact em values specified: padding, font-size, and border-radius.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button styling is incomplete or incorrect. Make sure you're using em units for all three properties with the values: padding: 0.75em 1.5em, font-size: 1em, border-radius: 0.5em.

steps.title: Add a media query to adjust root font size
steps.instruction: Add a media query that sets the html element's font-size to 18px for screens wider than 768px. This will affect all rem-based measurements on larger screens.
steps.hint: Use @media (min-width: 768px) { html { font-size: 18px; } } to target larger screens.
steps.expectedOutcome: A media query that changes the root font size to 18px on larger screens, making all rem-based measurements scale accordingly.
successCriteria: The media query targets screens wider than 768px and sets html { font-size: 18px; }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your media query uses (min-width: 768px) and sets font-size: 18px on the html element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: you need @media (min-width: 768px) { html { font-size: 18px; } }.

steps.title: Test the difference by changing parent font size
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to temporarily change the container's font-size to 20px to observe how em-based elements scale while rem-based elements stay the same.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule targeting the .container class and set its font-size property to 20px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container's font-size will be set to 20px, allowing you to see how elements using em units (like the span) scale relative to this new parent size while elements using rem units remain unaffected.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding font-size: 20px; to the .container rule. Check that the property name and value are correct.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. You need to add a CSS rule that sets the container's font-size to 20px. Look for the .container selector and add the font-size property.
